newsitem.title: ISRAEL: West Bank violence flares on "Land Day".
newsitem.headline: West Bank violence flares on "Land Day".

text.p: Stone-throwing Palestinians kept up street battles with Israeli soldiers on Sunday as Israel girded for possible violence by its own Arab citizens on an annual protest day against land expropriation.

But in some flashpoints in the West Bank, witnesses said Palestinian police intervened to stop demonstrators reaching Israeli positions on the 11th consecutive day of protests against Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
With pockets of violence still scattered across the West Bank, it was too soon to gauge whether the police action signalled the crackdown Israel has demanded from the Palestinian Authority.

"No one can imagine it is possible to advance towards peace while there is unrest, incitement, confrontation or, God forbid, terror," Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said after a two-day crisis mission by U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross.

Levy's office said the European Union's Middle East peace envoy, Miguel Angel Moratinos, delivered a message to the foreign minister from Yasser Arafat in which the Palestinian president pledged to do his best to curb violence.

The most serious clashes on Sunday erupted near the West Bank town of Jenin. Hospital officials said 25 Arabs were treated for rubber bullet wounds. Violence also flared in Hebron where eight Palestinians were wounded by rubber bullets.

The killing of a Palestinian by Israeli troops on Saturday -- which a Palestinian cabinet minister called an act of war -- raised tensions for Land Day, an annual day of protests by Israeli Arabs against land confiscation by the government.
Israeli police sent reinforcements to areas near Arab towns and villages inside Israel where marches were scheduled for later in the day. Some 850,000 Arabs live in the Jewish state.

Skirmishes continued near the tomb of the biblical matriarch Rachel in an Israeli enclave next to the self-ruled town of Bethlehem. Soldiers fired rubber bullets and teargas to keep the protesters back.

In Ramallah, north of Jerusalem, Palestinian police used clubs to disperse hundreds of protesters heading towards an Israeli roadblock, witnesses said. Protests erupted again and the army brought in a gravel cannon, which sprays pebbles.

Some 4,000 Arabs took part in a demonstration in Nablus. Israel deployed seven tanks at the entrance to the self-ruled town and two atop a hill overlooking Joseph's Tomb, a Jewish shrine in Nablus guarded by Israeli soldiers.
Palestinian police set up barriers that prevented protesters from marching towards the tomb, witnesses said.

"We want to have a sit-in near Joseph's Tomb as a peaceful protest against settlement policy. We do not want clashes here because any sacrifices would be in vain," said Husam Khader, a member of the Palestinian legislature from Nablus.
In Gaza, hundreds of Palestinian youths tried to march on an Israeli checkpoint but were held back by Palestinian police.
Soldiers patrolled streets of Israeli cities, on alert for suicide bombers nine days after a Moslem militant killed himself and three Israeli women in an attack on a cafe in Tel Aviv.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called on Israeli Arabs to shun violence on Land Day, which commemorates the 1976 killing by Israeli security forces of six Arabs protesting against expropriation of land by the government.

An Easter message by Michel Sabbah, Roman Catholic Patriarch in Jerusalem, focused on "the evil around us". He said: "Violence is still in the heart and blindness concerning the rights of others is still in the minds of leaders".
Hundreds of mourners marched in a funeral procession on Sunday for Abdullah Khalil Salah, 20, killed by Israeli gunfire on Saturday in clashes on the outskirts of Ramallah.
"No surrender," read one banner. Salah's body, held aloft by mourners, was wrapped in a Palestinian flag.

Salah was the first Palestinian killed in the clashes. He was buried in his home village of Beit Sahour which is next to Jabal Abu Ghneim, known as Har Homa in Hebrew, the site where Israel broke ground almost two weeks ago for a settlement of 6,500 homes for Jews, sparking the clashes.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak met Arafat in Cairo on Sunday for crisis talks on peace.

Arafat was also due to address a ministerial meeting of the Cairo-based Arab League which Egyptian newspapers said would issue a draft resolution calling on Arabs to suspend normalisation of ties with Israel until settlement work ceased.
